scope: Independent read-only review of final progress-only production integration: Controller, bubble overlay, native hooks, message-cell lifecycle and message gesture admission
review_activity: Read production source and existing native-playback evidence only; no source edits, test expansion, test execution or package build in this review step.

reviewed_behaviors.conclusion: Controller reads currentPlayingMsg/isMsgPlaying, int32 currentPlayTime and m_uiVoiceTime; seek uses uint32 milliseconds. It revalidates the active message/account, consumes generation before native seek and does not call rate/start/stop or mutate message/audio.

Fill is userInteractionEnabled=NO. Pan is attached to the content host, admits only a live matching bubble, rejects UIControl touches, requires horizontal intent and never delays unrecognized native touches. Vertical intent fails admission; navigation edge/pop gets priority. Recognized drag cancels the native click.
Existing message pan rejects touch points owned by active progress before starting; inactive voices and points outside the progress region retain the existing action path.

Overlay captures model/message pointer plus binding/generation and rechecks them throughout drag. Binding/reuse/disappearance/window removal/window hide detach the old state; geometry refresh follows native/time/merge/clown layout. End clears drag before potentially reentrant seek publication.

Settings changes invalidate controller and refresh/hide overlays; background blocks snapshots. Account nil/empty notification suspends snapshots even with an old still-playing same-account facade, and valid login notification restores only a new generation.

No added speed setting, rate mutation, thumb control or standalone slider; native rate/resume/transcribe controls retain their own touch regions. Existing forwarding preference versions remain independent.

verification_limit: Read-only code review confirms integration logic; actual iPhone native gesture arbitration, themed appearance and audible codec seek timing remain part of device verification. UI agent owns the bubble-pan regression result.
